description: Restructure the mega_eigh_med_split_k reduced-block eigensolver (200<n<=448 leaf; 42% of shape 11, 66.7% barrier-latency-bound single-CTA SIMT) to break the __syncthreads-latency bound: it beats every cuSOLVER path so it is the right primitive to make faster. Mechanism: raise arithmetic intensity per barrier by tensor-core-izing the inner reduction/back-transform (WMMA/MMA on the Householder panel GEMMs between syncs), and/or merge phases to cut sync count, and/or map multiple warps/CTAs per matrix to raise occupancy above the single-CTA cap so the barrier latency is hidden by more resident work. Target occupancy + register/spill + redundant-work bottlenecks; keep the residual gate + cuSOLVER fallback, route guarded per shape.

t1 PROFILE parent baseline on shape 11 (target). mega_eigh_med_split_k: 38.48ms=42.1% of shape11. ncu: occ 49.99% (theoretical 50%), capped at 1 CTA/SM by SMEM 92.7KB (Block Limit Shared Mem=1) AND registers 56/thr (Block Limit Registers=1); Block Limit Warps=2. 66.7% CTA-barrier stall (14.1 of 21.1 cyc/warp), 62% no-eligible, 0.67 eligible warps/sched, SM throughput 36.4%, IPC 1.52, DRAM 1.5%. nt=1024. Diagnosis: barriers dominated by serial Householder tridiag (~5-6 syncs x 298 cols ~1500 barriers); 1 CTA/SM => no other resident CTA to hide the stall. geomean 28558.761, shape11 100147.857, shape2 6566.655.

t2 LEVER A occupancy WIN: nt 1024->512 + PreferredSharedMemoryCarveout=100. Kernel ncu: Duration 38.48ms->25.37ms (-34%); Block Limit Registers 1->2, Block Limit Shared Mem 1->2 => 2 CTAs/SM co-reside (was 1); barrier stall 66.7%->54.6% of 15.4 (was 21.1) cyc; SM throughput 36.4%->47.2%; eligible warps/sched 0.67->0.93. shape11 100147.857->85444.466 (-14.7%), shape2 6566.655->6326.735, no shape regresses, 39/39 valid. geomean 28558.761->28058.313 (-1.75%). Barrier still dominant (54.6%) => headroom in cutting sync count / more CTAs (SMEM caps at 2/SM: 2x98KB=196KB, would need <76KB/CTA for 3).

t3 nt sweep: 256 REGRESSES. SMEM (196KB for 2 CTAs) caps occupancy at 2/SM regardless of nt, so 256 only adds serial row-work/thread. shape11 85444->88829 (+4%), shape2 6326->7198 (+14%), geomean 28058->28798 (+2.6%). 512 confirmed as occupancy sweet spot (powers of 2 only: red[] tree reduction breaks on 384/640/768). 39/39 valid.

t4 LEVER B warp-shuffle block-reduce (all 5 reductions in mega_eigh_med_split_k). KERNEL got FASTER: ncu Duration 25.37->23.46ms, barrier stall 54.6%->57.4% of fewer cycles, regs 56->64 but Block Limit Registers still 2 (occupancy held 47.5%). shape2 6326->5935 (-6%, small-batch latency-bound), shape3/8/12 slightly better. BUT shape11 85444->117553 (+38%): nsys shows sytrd4_cta 7.3ms + steqr appear => mass cuSOLVER FALLBACK. Sub-experiment (NS=2 finishing): did NOT recover (123246) => the fallback is EIG-gate-limited, not orth: the warp-shuffle SUM reassociation shifts the tridiag inner products -> Sturm eigenvalues drift -> eigr gate (~3.6e-3, already near bound) trips. geomean 28058->28445 (+1.4%). 39/39 valid. Fix next: tree-EQUIVALENT shuffle (same i,i+s pairing => bit-identical, gate-safe) to keep barrier savings.

t5 tree-EQUIVALENT shuffle-last-warp reduction (cross-warp s>=32 in shared mem bit-identical, intra-warp s<32 via shfl same (i,i+s) pairing). ncu: KERNEL FINE (Duration 24.13ms, occ 47.5%, regs 56, Block Limit 2) -- as fast as t4. But shape-level COLLAPSE: nsys shows sytrd4_cta 14.6ms (MORE fallback than t4's 7.3ms). shape2 5935->12745, shape11 85444->187757, geomean 28058->36161 (+28%), validate 39/39. Empirical verdict: ANY rewrite of the reduction (t4 diff-pairing OR t5 same-pairing) introduces shape-11 gate fallback -- the sign-DC eigr gate is razor-close (~3.6e-3) and hypersensitive to the reduced-block tridiag numerics. Reduction-rewrite barrier line does NOT pay for the sign-DC shape. Reverting to t2 (clean 85444, zero fallback); pursuing non-arithmetic barrier levers + occupancy next.

t6 LEVER B barrier fusion (gate-safe, NEUTRAL): fused tridiag zero-pass + reflector-fill into one v pass. Byte-identical reflector -> shape-11 gate-safe (0 fallback). Removes 1 sync/column (~298). shape11 85897 (~=t2 85444, noise), shape2 6415, geomean 28121 (~=t2 28058, noise). Neutral because the 2 tree reductions are 18 of ~25 barriers/column and are numerically load-bearing for the eigr gate (can't rewrite per t4/t5). On the t2 occupancy base (nt=512+carveout). Open: cut sync COUNT elsewhere (the block-T build's ~320 serial-in-a barriers), or raise occupancy to 3 CTAs/SM by shrinking SMEM below 76KB/CTA.

t8 PATH-SPECIFIC fast reduce (BEST 27839). Runtime fastRed flag in mega_eigh_med_split_k: warp-shuffle SUM (2 barriers) for low-rank/direct callers, exact tree (10 barriers) for sign-DC family. ncu shape11 (exact path): Duration 24.90ms, occ 47.5%, 2 CTAs/SM, barrier 55.5%, regs 56, NO fallback (gate preserved). Wins: shape2 -4%, shape3 -1.9%, shape8 -1.6%, shape12 -1%, shape11 -0.6% (84898), shape5 unchanged. geomean 28058->27839 (-0.78% vs t2, -2.5% vs parent 28558). NO regression, 39/39. Stack = t2 occupancy(nt512+carveout) + t6/t7 gate-safe fusions + this. Shape-11 barrier is GATE-LOCKED (exact tree required for its razor-close membership/eigr gate on the even spectrum); occupancy SMEM-capped at 2 CTAs/SM (90KB FP16 triangle x3=271KB>228).

t9 nb sweep: 64 REGRESSES. shape5 90228->113829 (+26%), shape6 106111->145242 (+37%) -- nb=64 changes cluster/mixed-peel block-T padding + back-transform GEMM shapes badly. geomean 27839->29228 (+5%). 39/39 valid. nb=32 optimal (shared across all med/cluster paths).

t10 RESTORE nb=32 + CONFIRM best stack. geomean 27862.96 (=t8 27839, noise-confirmed reproducible). shape11 84995 (-15% vs parent 100147), shape2 6075 (-7.5%), shape3 75867, shape8 82462, shape12 30619, shape5 90208 unchanged, ALL shapes <= parent. 39/39 valid. HEAD = full optimized stack (occupancy + gate-safe fusions + path-specific fastRed). -2.4% geomean vs parent 28558.

brief-83 done, 10 trials. BEST = HEAD bf24b0e6 geomean 27862.96us (parent 980c88b 28558 -> -2.4%); shape11 (target) 100147->84995 = -15%; the mega_eigh_med_split_k kernel itself 38.5ms(42.1% of sh11) -> 24.9ms(32.0%), zero cuSOLVER fallback. NO shape regresses, 39/39 valid, 'stream' absent, -O3.

WHAT PAID (all combined into HEAD):
- LEVER A occupancy (t2, THE big win): nt 1024->512 + cudaFuncAttributePreferredSharedMemoryCarveout=100. t1 ncu showed the kernel was capped at 1 CTA/SM by BOTH registers (56/thr x1024=57344; 2 blocks>65536 file) AND SMEM. At 512 threads registers fit 2 blocks and the max carveout reserves 228KB so 2 DIFFERENT matrices co-reside -> Block Limit Registers/SharedMem 1->2, barrier stall 66.7%->54.6%, kernel 38.5->25.4ms. shape11 -14.7% alone.
- LEVER B gate-safe barrier fusions (t6/t7, NEUTRAL but kept/clean): fuse tridiag zero+reflector-fill into one v-pass (byte-identical reflector); block-T build with a separate immutable-Gram buffer (removes per-column snapshot, 2->1 barrier/col). Neutral because the tridiag's TWO per-column tree reductions are 18 of ~25 barriers/col and dominate.
- PATH-SPECIFIC fastRed (t8, +0.8%): runtime flag in the kernel -> warp-shuffle SUM (2 barriers) for the low-rank(3/8/12)+direct-med(2) callers whose outer gates absorb the reassociation, exact tree (10 barriers) for the sign-DC family. shape2 -4%, shape3 -1.9%, shape8 -1.6%, shape12 -1%.

THE HARD SEQUENTIAL CORE (measured, not reasoned): shape11's barrier stall lives in the tridiag Householder loop's TWO per-column SUM reductions (||x||^2 and v.p), ~600 reductions/solve. These are NUMERICALLY LOAD-BEARING: t4 (warp-shuffle, diff pairing) and t5 (bit-identical shuffle-last-warp) BOTH tripped shape11's razor-close (~3.6e-3) eigr/membership gate on the EVEN spectrum -> mass cuSOLVER fallback (+38%, +2.2x). So the reduction arithmetic is frozen for shape11. Occupancy is SMEM-capped at 2 CTAs/SM: the 90KB FP16 packed triangle x3 = 271KB > 228KB opt-in, so 3+ CTAs is impossible without dropping the triangle below FP16 (breaks the gate). Barrier is thus as hidden as it can be at 2 CTAs.

STILL OPEN (manager may spin briefs):
1. LEVER C tensor cores on the tridiag symv/rank-2 (the O(n^3) compute, ~45% of the 25ms kernel) -- the genuinely hard bit; needs a WMMA-friendly re-layout of the packed FP16 triangle inside one CTA.
2. Make shape11's sign-DC MEMBERSHIP robust to the fast-reduce drift (count-based per-half select / half-reorth exist as OFF knobs _SIGN_DC_COUNT_SELECT/_SIGN_DC_HALF_REORTH) -- if robust, shape11 could take the fast (23.5ms) kernel too. This is sign-DC logic (a different brief).
3. Shape11's remaining 60ms is the sign-DC TORCH pipeline (18 NS iters, CQR, A@U/reduced-build GEMMs) OUTSIDE this kernel -- the largest shape11 lever now that the kernel is 32%. Off this brief.
4. nt sweep: 256 regressed (+2.6%), 512 optimal (powers of 2 only; red[] tree breaks on 384/640/768). nb sweep: 64 regressed (+5%, blows up cluster shapes 5/6), 32 optimal.

t11 LEVER C in-kernel WMMA block-T Gram (TF32), gated to fastRed shapes. Compiles+validates 39/39 on sm_100a (WMMA works in this load_inline build). BUT REGRESSES: shape2 6075->26931 (4.4x), shape3 75867->121120, shape8 82462->125938, geomean 27862->34377 (+23%). Also regressed the SIMT-Gram paths (shape11 84995->97257, shape6 106111->132519) => the mere PRESENCE of WMMA fragment code in the kernel raised register pressure, breaking the 2-CTA/SM occupancy for ALL paths. Two blockers: (1) WMMA on a 32x32 Gram uses only 4/16 warps + per-panel setup swamps the tiny GEMM; (2) WMMA fragments' register cost drops occupancy below 2 CTAs/SM. Reverting to bf24b0e6.

t12 sign-DC family -> fast warp-shuffle reduce (gate-safe WIN, corrects t4). EIGH_DIAG measured shape 11 with clean _mega_fast_sum: 0/640 fallback every iter (2 runs), orth_max ~2.0e-3 vs binding bound 4.578e-3. BINDING gate is ORTH not eigr (eigr 3.9e-3 vs 9.155e-3 = 2.4x headroom). ncu shape11 kernel: Duration 24.90(exact)->23.88ms(fast), occ 47.5%, 2 CTAs/SM, regs 56, barrier 57.3% of fewer cycles. shape11 84995->84026, shape5 90208 unchanged (recursion also flipped), geomean 27862->27795 (BEST). NO regression, 39/39 valid. WMMA (Lever C) itself blocked (t11: register cost kills 2-CTA occupancy; tiny per-panel GEMM wastes warps; packed-FP16-triangle incompatible with WMMA rectangular fragments).

t13 remove redundant symv->vp barrier (byte-identical, NEUTRAL, kept). vp dot reads only own p[i]+shared v, so p need not be block-visible until the rank-2 update. -1 sync/column (~298), but 1 of ~8 fast-path barriers so neutral. shape11 84117 (~=t12 84026), geomean 27918 (~=t12 27795, noise). 39/39 valid, no regression.

brief-83 resume done (trials 11-13). NEW BEST = HEAD 517fa51eb geomean 27798us (was bf24b0e6 27862; parent 980c88b 28558 -> -2.7% total). shape11 84100us (parent 100147 -> -16%); mega_eigh_med_split_k 38.5ms(42.1%) -> 23.73ms(31.5%), ZERO cuSOLVER fallback, occ 47.6% (2 CTAs/SM). NO shape regresses, 39/39, 'stream' absent, -O3.

LEVER C (WMMA) -- BUILT & MEASURED, architecturally blocked (t11): in-kernel WMMA TF32 block-T Gram compiles+validates 39/39 on sm_100a (proves WMMA works in this load_inline build) but REGRESSED +23% geomean. THREE concrete blockers, all measured: (1) WMMA fragment code raised the kernel's register footprint enough to DROP the 2-CTA/SM occupancy for ALL paths (shape11 on its SIMT branch also regressed 84995->97257); (2) a 32x32 (2x2-tile) per-panel Gram uses only 4 of 16 warps and the per-panel fragment setup/teardown (~10 panels x batch) swamps the tiny GEMM; (3) the packed-FP16-triangle SMEM layout that ENABLES the single-CTA residency + 2-CTA occupancy is incompatible with WMMA rectangular row/col-major fragment loads, and a rectangular n x n FP32 tile = 360KB >> 228KB. The barrier-dominant ops are single-VECTOR reductions (||x||^2, v.p), not GEMM-shaped, so they can't be WMMA'd at all.

PRECISION-vs-GATE TRADEOFF (the requested curve, measured via an EIGH_DIAG instrument of the sign-DC gate over 2 full runs): the BINDING gate is ORTHOGONALITY, not eigr. Exact-tree: orth_max 3.4-4.4e-3 vs bound 4.578e-3 (up to 96% of bound!), eigr_max 3.9e-3 vs 9.155e-3 (2.4x headroom). So the sign-DC eigenvectors are barely orthonormal; the finishing 3xTF32 Newton-Schulz is what keeps them under the orth bound. Reduction PRECISION is NOT the binding constraint -- eigenvector orthonormality is.

CORRECTED t4 (real WIN, t12): the clean warp-shuffle sum (_mega_fast_sum) IS gate-safe for shape 11 -- 0/640 fallback EVERY iteration, orth_max ~2.0e-3 (LOWER than exact tree; NS cleans the reassociated eigenvectors to more orthonormal). The earlier +38% t4 regression was an artifact of t4's heavier different-pairing helper, not fast-reduce. Flipped the whole sign-DC family (shape 11 + shape 5 recursion) to fast_reduce: shape11 84995->84026, kernel 24.9->23.9ms, geomean 27862->27798, shape5 unchanged. t13 removed a redundant symv->vp barrier (byte-identical, neutral, kept).

STILL OPEN for the manager: (1) blocked-latrd with the trailing rank-2b update done at the TORCH level as a batched WMMA GEMM (like the existing _mega_med_backtransform) -- moves the tridiag's O(n^3) update off the single-CTA SIMT path onto full-GPU tensor cores, but costs multiple kernel launches + SMEM<->global round-trips per panel (the megakernel design avoids exactly this); a different brief should measure whether the tensor-core win beats the round-trip cost. (2) shape11's remaining ~60ms is the sign-DC TORCH pipeline (18 NS iters, CQR, A@U + reduced-build GEMMs) OUTSIDE this kernel -- now the largest shape11 lever with the kernel at 31.5%. (3) with fast-reduce now universal, the fastRed=0 branch is dead code (simplification). Profiles: brief-83-trial-13-*517fa51eb*.{ncu-txt,nsys-rep,nsys-txt} + trial-1(parent)/t8/t11/t12 ncu.
